title: Radical Generosity
speaker: Ps Andrew Cartledge
blurb:
Generosity is easy to talk about. It gets a lot harder when it's actually costing you something.

Ps Andrew Cartledge draws on a church that had every reason not to give. The Macedonian believers were poor, under pressure and dealing with serious trouble of their own. And yet they begged Paul for the chance to participate. They weren't giving out of surplus. They were giving out of surrender, and that's what made it remarkable.

There's a moment in here about David raising an enormous offering for a temple he was never going to worship in, and what that says about the kind of generosity that actually changes things. And there's a question underneath all of it that's worth sitting with: are you asking God what to give, or are you asking God what he wants to do with you?

Those are very different questions.

title: Dig a Deeper Ditch
speaker: Ps Andrew Cartledge
blurb:
Three kings. An army without water. A valley without rain. And a prophet who says: dig ditches.

That is not the miracle. That is the job before the miracle.

Ps Andrew Cartledge takes a strange little passage from 2 Kings 3 and pulls out something that cuts against just about everything we assume about how God provides. The water was already coming. God had already spoken it. The digging wasn't what made it happen. But without the ditches, there was nowhere for it to go. Andrew takes that thought somewhere personal and sits it right in front of you: not whether God can provide, but whether you've actually made any room to receive it.

If your life is full to the edges with things that don't matter, that question lands a bit differently.
